key_insight: A DSL-guided multi-agent LLM system can improve inverse materials design by grounding natural-language rules in symbolic predicates and statistical evidence.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical way to discover candidate perovskite oxides for target properties without large task-specific datasets or retraining.
method: Translate design rules from natural language into chemistry DSL predicates
Use accumulated materials data to test, validate, and refine rules during the design loop
Run a multi-agent framework (ORCHESTRA) to search inverse designs for double perovskite oxides
evidence_signal: Compared with natural-language-only rules, the DSL-guided framework improved performance potential, especially for more challenging target properties, by helping the agent identify unsupported rules and update its rule store iteratively.
watch_item: Results are promising but depend on the quality of the DSL, the available materials data, and careful validation of generated candidates against real synthesis constraints.
paper_title: Symbolic Predicate-Guided Language Agents for Inverse Design of Perovskite Oxides
